brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A mountain tea made from the dried plant Sideritis raeseri, the Sideritis most often cultivated in Albania, Bulgaria, Greece and North Macedonia.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: The species is grown as a crop in these countries, where advanced hybrids also exist. It is planted in October to November or in February to March. Little more is documented about this tea as a drink.

images.author: Krzysztof Ziarnek, Kenraiz
images.alt: Pale yellow flowers of Sideritis raeseri on a stem in a botanical garden

harvest_season: Gathered in July, when the plant is in full bloom.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: A herbal infusion; the taste depends on the plant.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
